question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: a JSON-RPC initialize (protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0); content-type application/json, accept application/json, text/event-stream; no Authorization header, no x-api-key, no cookie

decoded.what-it-answered: one SSE frame of 404 bytes in 0.69 s: serverInfo name exa-search-server, title Exa, version 3.2.1, websiteUrl https://exa.ai; capabilities tools, prompts and resources, each with listChanged true; protocolVersion 2025-06-18 echoed. The response carried an mcp-session-id header (a UUID, redacted in the artifact).
decoded.what-this-measures: whether the vendor's hosted endpoint opens a session for a caller with no key, no OAuth token and no cookie. It does. The vendor's MCP page says 'No API key is required to get started' and its authentication table names a 'Keyless' mode as 'Free rate-limited usage without sign-in or API key'; the measurement agrees with the vendor's words.
decoded.session-as-observed: a session id was issued, but a later tools/list sent with no session header also answered 200 (the tools-list record), so the id is offered, not required; Hugging Face's server refuses without it, Astro's issues none.
decoded.version-as-observed: the handshake says 3.2.1; package.json on the source repository's main branch said 3.4.1 at 18:10Z the same day. Which build the hosted endpoint runs is the vendor's to say; the entry records both numbers and claims neither as the deployed version.
decoded.not-measured: any rate limit (no RateLimit header on this or any later response); what the OAuth or API-key modes add.
decoded.where-the-artifact-is: appendix dated 2026-10-03 (C) of the registry-sweep artifact linked below, section 1, headers and body whole, session id redacted.

finding: A keyless JSON-RPC initialize on https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp answered HTTP 200 on 2026-10-03 at 18:07:41Z in 0.69 s as text/event-stream: exa-search-server 3.2.1, protocol 2025-06-18, with a session id issued in the mcp-session-id header. No credential of any kind was sent. This matches the vendor's own authentication table, which names a Keyless mode ('Free rate-limited usage without sign-in or API key'); the rate limit's number is stated nowhere this researcher read and no RateLimit header was served.
